summary.headline: Centum Q2 FY27 revenue rose 52% YoY to INR 312 crore and PAT 77% to INR 23 crore; order book near INR 2,000 crore (+38%).
summary.overview: Standalone Q2 FY27 revenue was INR 312 crore (+52% YoY), with EBITDA of INR 40 crore (+63%, margin 12.69%, +87 bps) and PAT of INR 23 crore (+77%, margin 7.31%). H1 revenue rose 32% to INR 517 crore, H1 EBITDA rose 25% to INR 63 crore (margin 12.11%) and H1 PAT rose 28% to INR 36 crore. BTS revenue grew 84% in the quarter and EMS grew 41% YoY (about 42% QoQ). Management said the overseas subsidiaries were deconsolidated from Q1 FY27, so the consolidated numbers now reflect standalone. Supply-chain shortages (PCBs, memories, controllers, MLCCs) remain the main near-term constraint on lead times, prices and working capital.

financial_highlights.value: about INR 127 crore, incl. about INR 49 crore restricted

segments.name: BTS (Build to Spec: radar, electronics, space, defence)
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue +84% YoY; H1 +33% YoY. Order book INR 959 crore, +47% YoY. Wins include a ~INR 30 crore export EW subsystem order for a global OEM (naval ELINT) and a second tactical air navigation systems order of ~INR 51 crore (GRSE customer).

segments.name: EMS (Electronic manufacturing services)
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue +41% YoY and ~42% QoQ; H1 +32% YoY. Order book grew 30% YoY. Semiconductor equipment deliveries ramping; management sees the segment reaching a USD 45-50 million annual run-rate in about two years, versus an earlier USD 25-30 million estimate.

guidance_outlook: Medium-term revenue growth target of 25-30% CAGR; management said it could be closer to 30%. No specific quarterly or annual guidance given.
EBITDA margin target of 12.5-13% at company level for now, aiming to reach and breach 13% next year, then 14-15% in three to four years.
BTS margin range maintained at about 20-22% long term; quarterly BTS margins can swing on program mix.
H2 FY27 expected to be stronger than H1, with BTS order intake expected to be good in H2.
Order execution over roughly 2 to 2.5 years, with a non-linear ramp-up across the years.
capex_capacity: No near-term production capacity constraint, per management, but a new BTS facility is planned with system-level capability, dedicated test infrastructure and larger-system bay space.
Decision taken to set up an assembly, integration and test facility for full satellites in the new plant.
QIP capex portion of about INR 35 crore is almost fully utilised; the remaining capex spend is expected to complete in the current quarter.
Engineering bench strength being added to support design work on new systems.

Board approved (4 Nov 2026, subject to shareholder approval) raising the borrowing authorisation from INR 500 crore to INR 1,000 crore for additional non-fund-based limits; sanctioned limits of about INR 490 crore are nearly utilised.
demand_pricing: Supply chain is the principal near-term bottleneck: PCB lead times rose from 8-12 weeks to 40-50 weeks; memories, controllers and MLCCs are also short, driven by AI/data-centre demand and Middle East/Europe logistics issues.
Component price increases, higher inventory needs and working capital pressure are flowing through; the company is buying and stocking parts for roughly 12 months of demand.
Q2 BTS margin was held back by a higher material-cost program mix versus last year.

Semiconductor EMS demand is rising almost quarterly for qualified products; the anchor customer is displacing an incumbent operating in Southeast Asia. Management said preliminary talks with other customers are far behind the anchor's traction.

Three new EMS customers: a global tier-1 transport OEM (braking and platform-door controllers, first Indian EMS partner); a German industrial machinery OEM (metrology, first Indian EMS partner); and a Middle East defence customer (drones, design-led, serial orders started, at least USD 10 million per year each once ramped in two to three years).

Global BTS: first Middle East subsystem-level customer and advanced talks with a European customer, both requiring in-country IP. Management said it would sell full systems abroad only after Indian deployment, two to three years away.

Defence exports are targeted at about INR 50,000 crore nationally versus about INR 38,000 crore currently (BTS plus build-to-print). Order mix for the next two to three years expected at about 60% defence and 40% space.

qa_highlights.question: Would the company revise full-year growth guidance given H1 and the order book?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give specific annual guidance, but reiterated a 25-30% medium-term growth target and said visibility is good.

qa_highlights.question: Why hasn't BTS strength lifted margins?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said BTS margins are about 20-22% long term and quarterly swings reflect program mix. Q2 had higher material cost in some programs. Company-level margin target is 12.5-13%.

qa_highlights.question: Was BTS Q2 growth a spillover from Q1?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said no. It reflects higher execution and activity given the larger order book, though quarterly variation is normal, and H2 should be stronger than H1.

qa_highlights.question: Capacity bottlenecks and revenue phasing on the BTS order book?
qa_highlights.answer: No short-term production constraint. Engineering headcount is being added, and a new BTS facility with system-level test infrastructure is planned. Revenue will ramp unevenly over about 2 to 2.5 years.

qa_highlights.question: Inventory build and use of the INR 50 crore QIP balance?
qa_highlights.answer: Supply chain constraints (PCB lead times of 40-50 weeks, memory shortages) drove the inventory build. About 50% of net inventory is covered by customer prepayments. INR 50.7 crore of QIP is held as general corporate reserve for future strategic plans.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook beyond FY27 and what are the margin ambitions?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said revenue CAGR of about 25-30%, closer to 30%. Margins are targeted at 12.5-13% now, with 13% next year and 14-15% in three to four years.

risks_watch: Component shortages and long lead times (PCBs, memories, controllers, MLCCs) could delay EMS and BTS deliveries and keep raising working capital.
Inventory of about INR 540 crore and receivable days of 106 depend on customer prepayments (about 50% coverage of net inventory).
Quarterly BTS margin volatility from program mix; the company guides to 20-22% over the long run.
Semiconductor EMS growth is concentrated in one anchor customer; the USD 45-50 million run-rate depends on it.
Borrowing authorisation increase to INR 1,000 crore needs shareholder approval; utilisation of non-fund-based limits to watch.
Timing of satellite and turnkey opportunities and the GRSE-linked ship programmes is unclear; management could not yet quantify the value.
summary.management_tone: Confident on demand, order book and medium-term growth, but deliberately non-committal on specific quarterly or annual numbers. Candid that supply-chain bottlenecks are the main near-term constraint. Evasive on the timing and size of several new opportunities (global BTS, satellites, GRSE ship programmes).
key_quotes: Overall, the company delivered a strong performance during the quarter, supported by robust execution across both BTS and EMS.
Supply chain, however, remains the principal near-term bottleneck.
So, I would not read this as a one -off sort of spike in the revenue or a spillover from Q1, but a more reflection of the higher level of execution and activity in this business.
At the company level, we will strive towards reaching and breaching the 13% mark at a combined level.

adds.what: New BTS facility with system-level capability, dedicated test infrastructure and larger-system bay space, plus full-satellite assembly, integration and test fac

growth.why: Medium-term guide of 25-30% CAGR (could be near 30%) held, backed by order book of about INR 2,000 crore (+38% YoY, BTS book INR 959 crore +47%) and Q2 revenue +52%; new BTS facility capex is planned but its size and timing are not given, and no specific annual guidance was set.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Company EBITDA margin 12.69% in Q2 (+87 bps YoY) and H1 12.11%, with management guiding 12.5-13% now, 13% next year and 14-15% in three to four years; Q2 BTS margin was held back by material-cost mix, so the expansion path is guided but not yet visible in the quarters.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: A new BTS facility with system-level test infrastructure and full-satellite AIT is approved, and QIP capex of about INR 35 crore is almost fully used with the rest completing this quarter; management says there is no near-term production constraint, so commissioning is probably beyond the 2-4 quarter window.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Order book about INR 2,000 crore (+38% YoY), BTS book INR 959 crore (+47%), H1 revenue +32% and management expects H2 stronger than H1 with good BTS order intake.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Capacity is not described as constrained, but the board has approved raising borrowing authority from INR 500 crore to INR 1,000 crore and sanctioned non-fund limits of about INR 490 crore are nearly used, so further capex and working-capital funding are likely to follow.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management declined annual guidance but says the 25-30% CAGR could be closer to 30%, and the semicon EMS run-rate view rose from USD 25-30 million to USD 45-50 million.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: PCB lead times rose from 8-12 weeks to 40-50 weeks and inventory is about INR 540 crore with 136 NWC days, so delivery slippage and working-capital strain could hit near-term numbers even though guidance is held.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Management cited a Middle East defence drone customer with serial orders started, a first Middle East subsystem-level BTS customer and talks with a European customer, but gave no launch dates or sizes.

rows.label: Semicon EMS anchor-customer ramp to USD 45-50M run-rate
rows.why: Management raised the view from USD 25-30M to USD 45-50M run-rate, with semiconductor EMS demand rising almost quarterly, but this depends on one anchor customer.

rows.label: Three new EMS customers ramping
rows.why: Tier-1 transport, German industrial and Middle East defence customers have started or are starting serial orders, with each Middle East customer expected at least USD 10M per year once ramped in two to three years.

rows.label: Working capital pressure from component stocking
rows.why: The company is stocking about 12 months of parts, inventory is about INR 540 crore, and NWC days are 136 even after improving 6 days, so funding needs stay elevated.

tone.note: Management was confident on demand, the order book and the 25-30% growth target, but would not give annual numbers and was candid about PCB and memory shortages. Analysts pressed on BTS margins held back by mix, whether Q2 BTS growth was a Q1 spillover, and the revenue phasing on the order book.
